title_en: Shaanxi Chongli Industrial Development Co., Ltd. v. China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Shaanxi Branch and Xi'an Jiajia Real Estate Comprehensive Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over third-party objection to enforcement
ruling_gist_en: A third party who files an action for execution objection shall bear the burden of proof to show that it has a civil right or interest in the subject matter of execution sufficient to exclude the enforcement, and the standard of proof must reach a high probability that the right or interest excludes the enforcement.
keywords_en: Civil; Third-party action for execution objection; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Shaanxi Province; Legal person; Financial institution; Property Law; Civil Procedure Law; Burden of proof in a third-party action for execution objection; Determination of ownership of unregistered immovable property; Ownership of house developed under a joint development agreement; Reversal on appeal; Execution objection; Joint development of real estate; Confirmation of house ownership; Principle of property rights publicity; Good faith
full_text_en:
Shaanxi Chongli Industrial Development Co., Ltd. v.
China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Shaanxi Branch,
and Xi'an Jiajia Real Estate Comprehensive Development Co., Ltd.
— Action for Execution Objection by a Person Other Than the Party Involved

【Ruling Summary】

A person other than the party involved who files an action for execution objection shall bear the burden of proof to demonstrate that he or she has a civil right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement on the subject matter of execution, and must satisfy the high degree of probability standard of proof that the right or interest precludes enforcement.

In an action for execution objection, the parties with opposing interests and claims are first the person other than the party involved and the applying enforcement creditor. The admission of facts by the person subject to enforcement may be used as evidence for finding the facts of the case, but such admission cannot, by itself, exempt the person other than the party involved from his or her burden of proof.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Appeal No. 763

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Shaanxi Branch, domiciled at Building No. 10, South Street, Beilin District, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.
Person in charge: Li Xiaozhao, General Manager of the Branch.
Agent ad litem: Guo Xianglong, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Beijing).
Agent ad litem: Huang Xingchao, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Xi'an).

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Shaanxi Chongli Industrial Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 3-1, Building 19, Ziwei Garden, High-tech Zone, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.
Legal representative: Liu Chongli, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Liu Cong, lawyer of Beijing Dentons (Xi'an) Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Yu Fei, lawyer of Beijing Dentons (Xi'an) Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xi'an Jiajia Real Estate Comprehensive Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 31, West Section of North Second Ring Road, Weiyang District, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.
Legal representative: Li Shilong, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Yang Jiancheng, lawyer of Shaanxi Jingyuan Xinyan Law Firm.

The appellant, China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Shaanxi Branch (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Shaanxi Branch), filed an appeal against the civil judgment (2015) Shaanxi Civil First Instance No. 00037 rendered by the Shaanxi High People's Court in the case of Shaanxi Chongli Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chongli Company) v. Xi'an Jiajia Real Estate Comprehensive Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiajia Company) concerning an action for execution objection by a person other than the party involved. This Court accepted the case on November 22, 2016, formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, and held a hearing. Guo Xianglong and Huang Xingchao, agents ad litem of Cinda Shaanxi Branch; Liu Cong and Yu Fei, agents ad litem of Chongli Company; and Yang Jiancheng, agent ad litem of Jiajia Company, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now concluded.

Cinda Shaanxi Branch requested on appeal: (1) to set aside the civil judgment (2015) Shaanxi Civil First Instance No. 00037; (2) to dismiss the claims of Chongli Company; and (3) to order Chongli Company to bear the litigation costs of this case. Facts and reasons: (1) The properties involved in this case have not yet been registered for real estate. Their state-owned land use right certificate, construction land planning permit, construction project planning permit, construction permit, commodity housing pre-sale permit, and other related approval procedures and construction design schemes are all registered under the name of Jiajia Company. Pursuant to the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Execution Objection and Reconsideration Cases by People's Courts (hereinafter referred to as the Provisions on Execution Objection and Reconsideration), paragraph 1 of Article 25, the evidence submitted by Chongli Company is insufficient to prove that it is the owner of the properties involved. The joint development agreement between Chongli Company and Jiajia Company establishes a contractual relationship and a distribution of sales proceeds (a debtor-creditor relationship) between the two parties, which is an ordinary creditor's right. Chongli Company does not have a real right or a right to claim a real right over the properties sealed by the enforcement court. The establishment, modification, and transfer of real rights in immovable property take effect upon registration; without registration, no effect on real rights in immovable property occurs. (2) The original judgment found unclear facts and incorrectly applied the law. According to the agreement, Chongli Company, as the investor, should contribute funds and bear all construction and installation costs within the design blueprints. The first-instance court did not ascertain Chongli Company's investment actions or whether it had fully performed the obligations stipulated in the agreement. The "builder" of the project involved should be Jiajia Company, the title holder under the five permits, not Chongli Company, which only assumed corresponding investment rights and obligations under the contract. The distribution of properties agreed between Chongli Company and Jiajia Company is itself a form of benefit distribution in joint development; without registration of the real right, it should not produce real right effects. A cooperative party that has not been registered in accordance with the law does not have a real right over the developed land or the properties built thereon. Claiming ownership of immovable property and precluding court enforcement based solely on a written agreement violates the basic principles of statutory real rights and public notice of real rights. The original judgment erroneously applied the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Property Law), Article 30. The original judgment determined that the properties involved were jointly owned by Jiajia Company and Chongli Company, but the operative part of the judgment ruled that the ownership of the properties involved belonged to Chongli Company, which is contradictory.

Chongli Company argued in defense: (1) The registration of the five permits under Jiajia Company's name cannot deny Chongli Company's ownership of the properties involved. The determination of ownership under Article 25 of the Provisions on Execution Objection and Reconsideration, which primarily relies on formal review supplemented by substantive review, applies only to the execution objection procedure and merely specifies that ownership of the subject matter of execution should generally be determined based on registration and possession. The original judgment correctly confirmed Chongli Company's ownership of the properties involved based on the relevant agreements between Chongli Company and Jiajia Company. (2) Chongli Company and Jiajia Company have signed agreements regarding the construction and distribution of the properties involved and have actually performed them. The original judgment correctly applied Article 30 of the Property Law in determining the ownership of the properties involved. (3) Cinda Shaanxi Branch's claim for enforcement of the properties involved violates the principles of good faith and fairness.

Jiajia Company argued in defense: The original judgment's application of Article 30 of the Property Law, which expanded the interpretation of not requiring registration as a condition for obtaining ownership of immovable property, and its determination that Chongli Company and Jiajia Company jointly owned the properties involved from the time of completion were erroneous. Chongli Company does not have legal ownership of the properties involved.

Chongli Company filed a complaint with the first-instance court requesting: (1) confirmation that Chongli Company has ownership of the 10 properties (10-11105, 10-11205, 10-10906, 10-21110, 10-21310, 10-21410, 10-21710, 11-20803, 11-20105, 11-20106, with a total value of approximately RMB 4,500,000) located in Buildings No. 10 and No. 11 of Jiajia SPORT at the intersection of North Second Ring Road and Wenjing Road, Xi'an Economic and Technological Development Zone; (2) an order that the above properties shall not be enforced and that the seizure of the above properties be lifted; and (3) an order that Cinda Shaanxi Branch and Jiajia Company bear the litigation costs of this case.

The first-instance court found the following facts: On September 3 and 6, 2004, Jiajia Company and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd., Xi'an Zhuque Street Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Zhuque Street Sub-branch) respectively entered into the Real Estate Loan Contracts No. 002 and No. 003 (Shaanxi Gongyin Ying Zhuque Jingzi) and the Mortgage Contracts No. 004 and No. 005 (Shaanxi Gongyin Ying Zhuque Dizi). Jiajia Company borrowed a total of RMB 80,000,000 yuan from ICBC Zhuque Street Sub-branch, with a loan term of 30 months. Jiajia Company provided as mortgage security the construction in progress of Buildings 3, 4, and 5 of Wenjing Garden, located west of Wenjing Road, Xi'an Economic and Technological Development Zone. On September 10, 2004, Xi'an Hantang Notary Public Office (formerly Shaanxi Notary Public Office) notarized the above contracts and issued notarial certificates with enforceability, respectively numbered (2004) Shaanxi Zheng Jing Zi No. 6526 and No. 6527. On January 10, 2007, Xi'an Hantang Notary Public Office issued execution certificates No. (2007) Shaanxi Zheng Zhi Zi No. 1 and No. 2, granting enforceability to the principal and interest owed by Jiajia Company totaling RMB 85,592,366.6 yuan.

On February 6, 2007, ICBC Zhuque Street Sub-branch applied to the first-instance court for compulsory enforcement. On February 14 of the same year, the first-instance court accepted the case for enforcement, with case numbers (2007) Shaanxi Zhi Er Gong Zi No. 58 and No. 59. During the enforcement, the first-instance court found that, except for 46 units of the loan mortgage property (Buildings 3, 4, and 5 of Wenjing Garden) that had not been sold and were seized by the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court, the remaining units had all been sold. Upon the application of ICBC Zhuque Street Sub-branch, the first-instance court carried out a subsequent seizure of the above 46 units and seized the land use right of 9,589.1 square meters and the construction in progress (above-ground buildings: Blocks A and D of Jiajia Times Square) located on the north side of North Second Ring Road, Weiyang District, Xi'an, as well as the land use right of 16,497 square meters and the construction in progress (above-ground buildings: Blocks B and C of Jiajia Times Square), and also seized 428 underground parking spaces covering an area of 12,295.18 square meters located in Wenjing Garden. Later, upon the application of ICBC Zhuque Street Sub-branch, the first-instance court lifted the seizure on the land use right of 16,497 square meters and the construction in progress. During the enforcement process, the first-instance court transferred the above 428 underground parking spaces to ICBC Zhuque Street Sub-branch to offset the debts owed by Jiajia Company, and auctioned one of the subsequently seized 46 units according to law. In Case No. 59, the remaining outstanding creditor's right principal was RMB 12,740,000 yuan and corresponding interest. On March 16, 2009, the first-instance court ruled to consolidate the remaining creditor's right principal of RMB 12,740,000 yuan and corresponding interest from Case No. 59 with Case No. 58 for enforcement, and Case No. 59 was terminated. On April 20 of the same year, the first-instance court ruled to terminate the enforcement because the land use right of 9,589.1 square meters and the construction in progress belonging to Jiajia Company that had been seized were not in a condition for enforcement, after soliciting the opinion of the applying enforcement creditor, ICBC Zhuque Street Sub-branch.

Subsequently, due to internal reorganization within ICBC, the business of ICBC Zhuque Street Sub-branch was transferred to ICBC Xi'an South Street Sub-branch. Later, the creditor's right in this case was adjusted to be handled by ICBC East Street Sub-branch. On March 23, 2011, ICBC East Street Sub-branch applied to resume enforcement. On April 6, 2011, the first-instance court accepted the resumed enforcement. During the enforcement process, the first-instance court offset the first and second floors of Block A of Jiajia Times Square, which had been seized, to ICBC East Street Sub-branch at a price of RMB 91,380,430 yuan, to satisfy the loan principal and double interest for delayed performance during the period of delay, totaling RMB 91,316,014 yuan. The excess amount of RMB 64,410 yuan was to be refunded by ICBC East Street Sub-branch to Jiajia Company upon the handover of the properties. On December 27, 2012, the first-instance court ruled to lift the seizure on the properties on the fourth floor of Block A and the first floor of Block D of Jiajia Times Square and the corresponding land use right, and the enforcement was terminated.

On October 16, 2013, ICBC East Street Sub-branch filed an application with the first-instance court to resume enforcement, claiming a calculation error. On December 13 of the same year, the first-instance court accepted the resumed enforcement. On March 3, 2014, the first-instance court seized the properties located in Blocks B and C of Jiajia Times Square, No. 31, West Section of North Second Ring Road, Xi'an Economic and Technological Development Zone, with the following unit numbers: 10-11105, 10-11205, 10-10906, 10-21110, 10-21310, 10-21410, 10-21710, 11-12302, 11-10104, 11-10706, 11-10408, 11-20803, 11-20105, 11-20106, and 11-20107.

Separately, on January 13, 2015, Cinda Shaanxi Branch submitted an application to the first-instance court stating that it had entered into a creditor's rights transfer agreement with ICBC East Street Sub-branch on December 8, 2014, to lawfully transfer the loan creditor's right for which ICBC East Street Sub-branch had applied to resume enforcement, and requested that it be substituted as the applying enforcement creditor. Subsequently, the first-instance court ruled to substitute Cinda Shaanxi Branch as the applying enforcement creditor.

On June 15, 2015, Chongli Company filed an execution objection with the first-instance court as a person other than the party involved. On September 17 of the same year, the first-instance court issued the enforcement ruling (2015) Shaanxi Zhi Yi Zi No. 00002, holding that Chongli Company did not have the relevant property registration procedures or property ownership certificates or other ownership documentation. The properties subject to the objection had not yet been registered for real estate, and their state-owned land use certificate, construction project planning permit, and other related approval procedures and construction design schemes were all registered under the name of the person subject to enforcement, Jiajia Company. According to the Provisions on Execution Objection and Reconsideration, when a person other than the party involved raises an objection, the people's court shall determine whether such person is the title holder based on the following criteria: for registered immovable property, based on the real estate register; for unregistered buildings, structures, and ancillary facilities, based on the land use right register, construction project planning permit, construction permit, and other relevant evidence. The evidence provided by Chongli Company was insufficient to prove that it was the owner of the properties involved, so the court rejected Chongli Company's objection. Chongli Company, dissatisfied, filed a lawsuit with the first-instance court, leading to the present case.

The first-instance court also found that on July 19, 2006, Chongli Company and Jiajia Company entered into the Joint Development Contract for the B and C Blocks of Jiajia Times Square Project, stipulating that the two parties would jointly construct residential buildings in Blocks B and C and the underground parking garage north of Block B, with a total joint construction area of 85,000 square meters. Jiajia Company would provide the construction project land, project planning approval procedures, construction design schemes, and construction drawings, while Chongli Company would contribute capital in RMB and bear all construction and installation costs within the project design blueprints. When the total joint investment of the two parties reached 25% to 30% of the total project price, Jiajia Company should unconditionally transfer the project to Chongli Company, which would then independently construct, operate, and sell, with all proceeds belonging to Chongli Company. The investment and return to be recovered by Jiajia Company were RMB 700 yuan per square meter of the total construction area, and RMB 1,250 yuan per square meter for the first to third floor podiums of Block B. The remaining investment, sales of units, property rights (same term as land use right), and income would all belong to Chongli Company.

On June 19, 2007, Jiajia Company issued an authorization letter stating: "After deliberation by Jiajia Company, it has decided to entrust Chongli Company with the full authority to sell Blocks B and C of Jiajia Times Square. The personal housing loans and margin for units in Blocks B and C shall be directly transferred to Chongli Company's account."

On December 2, 2008, Jiajia Company and Chongli Company submitted a Statement of Explanation to the Xi'an Housing Provident Fund Management Center, stating: "The Jiajia Times Square project developed by our company is a joint development with the investor Chongli Company. The preliminary approval procedures were all carried out in the name of Jiajia Company. For the later sales, our company entrusted Chongli Company to be responsible for the sales and collection of payments for Buildings No. 10 and No. 11. Therefore, the down payment receipts for the buyers of these two buildings were all issued by Chongli Company, and the provident fund loans for the buyers were also transferred to Chongli Company's account."

On September 7, 2009, Chongli Company and Jiajia Company entered into the Agreement on Relevant Issues Concerning the Joint Development Contract for the B and C Blocks of Jiajia Times Square Project, which stated that the project had been completed and accepted after inspection. Both parties confirmed that Chongli Company had paid all investment returns to Jiajia Company in full in accordance with the contract, and that there were no further disputes between the parties regarding the distribution of contract returns. Both parties confirmed that Chongli Company, in accordance with the contract, lawfully and without dispute owned all property rights of Blocks B and C of Jiajia Times Square and the underground parking garage as agreed in the contract, as well as all sales proceeds after the transfer of the property rights.

The Blocks B and C of Jiajia Times Square as agreed in the contract between Jiajia Company and Chongli Company are the properties in Buildings No. 10 and No. 11 of Jiajia SPORT. The state-owned land use right certificate, construction land planning permit, construction project planning permit, construction permit, and other procedures for the Jiajia Times Square project are all under the name of Jiajia Company.

The first-instance court held that an action for execution objection by a person other than the party involved refers to an action in which such person claims to have a right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement on the subject matter of execution and requests the court to prohibit enforcement of that subject matter. This case is an action for execution objection filed by Chongli Company as a person other than the party involved, requesting confirmation of its ownership of the ten properties involved and an order that the properties shall not be enforced and that the seizure be lifted. Whether the claims can be sustained depends on whether Chongli Company legally owns the ten properties involved or has other civil rights or interests sufficient to preclude enforcement, and consequently whether enforcement should be prevented.

Article 30 of the Property Law provides: "A real right established or extinguished by a factual act such as the lawful construction or demolition of a house shall take effect upon completion of the factual act." The lawful construction of a house is a factual act that gives rise to a right. Upon completion, the house factually creates ownership, and the builder thereby acquires ownership of the house. This acquisition is a mode of original acquisition under Article 30 of the Property Law, which does not require registration as a condition for obtaining ownership. Jiajia Company and Chongli Company are in a joint development relationship, jointly contributing to the development and construction of the properties involved. Therefore, both Jiajia Company and Chongli Company are builders of the properties, and from the time of completion, they should jointly own the properties involved. The Agreement on Relevant Issues Concerning the Joint Development Contract for the B and C Blocks of Jiajia Times Square Project entered into on September 7, 2009, confirmed that Chongli Company had paid all investment returns to Jiajia Company, and that Chongli Company owned all property rights of Blocks B and C of Jiajia Times Square and the underground parking garage agreed in the contract, as well as all sales proceeds after the transfer of the property rights. The above agreement between Jiajia Company and Chongli Company constitutes a division of the jointly owned property. This agreement represents the true intention of both parties, does not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and is therefore valid. The ten properties in dispute in this case belong to Chongli Company. Chongli Company's request for confirmation of its ownership of these ten properties is legally justified and should be supported. Cinda Shaanxi Branch argues that the state-owned land use right certificate, construction project planning permit, and other certificates are all under the name of Jiajia Company, and that under Article 25 of the Provisions on Execution Objection and Reconsideration, Jiajia Company should be the title holder. However, that judicial interpretation applies to enforcement proceedings. The examination and determination of ownership of the properties involved in this case in the execution objection stage is merely a preliminary review. The first-instance court's determination, based on the underlying transaction facts found in the litigation proceedings, that Chongli Company is the owner of the properties involved is not inconsistent with the above judicial interpretation. Cinda Shaanxi Branch's defense on this ground cannot stand. Cinda Shaanxi Branch only holds an ordinary monetary creditor's right against Jiajia Company. This ordinary creditor's right cannot prevail against Chongli Company's real right of ownership over the properties involved.

According to Article 312 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, "With respect to an action for objection to enforcement brought by a third party, the People's Court shall, after trial, handle the matter according to the following circumstances: (1) If the third party has a civil right and interest in the subject matter of enforcement sufficient to preclude enforcement, the court shall rule that the subject matter of enforcement shall not be enforced; (2) If the third party does not have a civil right and interest in the subject matter of enforcement sufficient to preclude enforcement, the court shall rule to dismiss the claims. If the third party simultaneously makes a claim for confirmation of its rights, the People's Court may render a ruling on that claim in its judgment." In this case, Chongli Company lawfully owns the ten sets of houses involved in the case, which is sufficient to preclude enforcement. Therefore, in accordance with the above provisions, these ten sets of houses shall not be enforced. As for Chongli Company's request to lift the seal-up of the ten sets of houses involved, such a request should be made in the enforcement proceedings and is not addressed in this case.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 30 of the Property Law and Article 312 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled as follows: (1) Chongli Company has ownership of the ten sets of houses located at the Jiajia Times Square, at the intersection of Beierhuan and Wenjing Road, Xi'an Economic and Technological Development Zone (units 10-11105, 10-11205, 10-10906, 10-21110, 10-21310, 10-21410, 10-21710, 11-20803, 11-20105, 11-20106). (2) In the case where Shaanxi Branch of Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd. filed an application for enforcement against Jiajia Company, the above ten sets of houses shall not be enforced. The case acceptance fee of RMB 42,800 shall be borne jointly by Shaanxi Branch of Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd. and Jiajia Company.

During the second instance of this court, the parties submitted evidence in accordance with law regarding their grounds of appeal, and this court conducted an exchange of evidence and cross-examination. Shaanxi Branch of Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd. submitted the Entrustment Letter for Appraisal (No. [2014] Shan-Ji-Wei-Zi No. 4-2) from the court of first instance and the Real Estate Appraisal Report from Shaanxi Jinda Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd., to prove that Jiajia Company used one of the houses to repay a debt, making it the property rights holder of the houses involved; the real estate appraisal report indicated that eight of the houses involved were vacant with unfinished walls and floors, and two were rented out, and that Chongli Company did not actually occupy the houses. Chongli Company acknowledged the authenticity of this evidence but did not accept its purpose of proof; Jiajia Company, in its cross-examination, stated that it acknowledged the authenticity, and the purpose of proof should be determined by the court. This court confirms the authenticity of these two pieces of evidence, but the matter entrusted by the court of first instance was the appraised value of the fifteen houses; the debt repayment and occupation status of the houses are factual issues, which are neither within the scope of the entrustment by the court of first instance nor part of the commissioned appraisal content, and are irrelevant to the facts to be proved. Therefore, this court does not admit this evidence.

At the trial of the second instance, Jiajia Company stated that after the judgment of the first instance, the general property ownership certificates for the houses involved had been processed under the name of Jiajia Company. Due to special reasons, the legal representative of Jiajia Company had not yet received the property ownership certificates; the general certificates were given to a minority shareholder of Jiajia Company.

At the trial of the second instance, the collegiate panel asked Chongli Company: "During the first instance, did Chongli Company submit evidence materials regarding the investment in Buildings B and C?" Chongli Company replied: "No, because according to the agreement signed between the parties, the evidence submitted by the first instance was acknowledged by Jiajia Company regarding our investment and construction, we believed that was sufficient to prove that the contract had been performed." The collegiate panel asked: "During the second instance, can you submit evidence of the investment and construction?" Chongli Company replied: "Because it has been a long time, we will look for relevant evidence after the trial." However, to date, no such evidence has been submitted.

This court confirms the other facts found by the court of first instance.

This court holds that, based on the parties' grounds of appeal, factual reasons, and defense opinions, the focus of the dispute in this case is: whether the original judgment was correct in finding that Chongli Company had ownership of the ten sets of houses involved and could preclude enforcement.

First, generally, the creation of real property rights in immovables requires registration to take effect. In accordance with the principle of legality of property rights stipulated in the Property Law, the types and content of property rights are prescribed by law and cannot be created by the parties themselves. Article 9 of the Property Law provides that the creation, alteration, transfer, and extinction of real property rights in immovables shall take effect upon registration in accordance with law; without registration, they shall not take effect, unless otherwise provided by law. Article 14 of the Property Law provides that the creation, alteration, transfer, and extinction of real property rights in immovables that are required to be registered by law shall take effect upon entry in the real estate register. According to the facts found, the houses involved were not registered under the name of Chongli Company, and Chongli Company cannot obtain ownership of the houses involved based on registration.

Second, can Chongli Company obtain ownership of the houses involved based on lawful construction? This court holds that, first, Article 142 of the Property Law provides that the ownership of buildings, structures, and ancillary facilities constructed by the holder of the construction land use right belongs to the holder of the construction land use right, unless there is contrary evidence. That is, the ownership of buildings, structures, and ancillary facilities constructed by the holder of the construction land use right generally belongs to that holder. In this case, the holder recorded in the construction land use right certificate is Jiajia Company, not Chongli Company. Second, although Article 30 of the Property Law provides that property rights created or extinguished by factual acts such as lawful construction or demolition of buildings shall take effect upon the completion of such factual acts, obtaining property rights through lawful construction must meet two prerequisites: first, there must be lawful construction procedures, completion of specific approvals, obtaining lawful land rights, and compliance with planning requirements; second, the building must be completed. According to the facts found, the state-owned land use right certificate, construction land planning permit, construction project planning permit, construction permit, etc., for the houses involved all record the rights holder as Jiajia Company. That is, during the project initiation, planning, and construction process of the houses involved, Jiajia Company was the construction party determined by the relevant administrative approval authorities; Chongli Company, based solely on its joint construction agreement with Jiajia Company, cannot be directly deemed as the lawful constructor under Article 30 of the Property Law, nor does it automatically obtain property rights due to factual acts. Analyzing the content of the "Joint Development Contract for Jiajia Times Square Buildings B and C and the Underground Garage Project North of Building B," when both parties' joint investment reached 25% to 30% of the total project cost, Jiajia Company was obligated to transfer the project unconditionally to Chongli Company, who would then independently construct, operate, and sell, with all proceeds belonging to Chongli Company, and the taxes and fees for the transfer would be borne by Chongli Company. That is, both Chongli Company and Jiajia Company were aware that, under their cooperative development, Chongli Company could only participate in the distribution of completed houses based on the joint construction agreement, and the project transfer still required relevant approval procedures.

Third, Article 311 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that when a third party or the applying enforcement party brings an action for objection to enforcement, the third party shall bear the burden of proof to show that it has a civil right and interest in the subject matter of enforcement sufficient to preclude enforcement. Chongli Company, claiming that it has ownership of the houses involved based on lawful construction, must bear the burden of proof. Since it has neither submitted sufficient evidence to prove the facts of its investment in the project involved, nor submitted evidence to prove its right of occupancy over the houses involved, nor submitted evidence to prove that the houses involved have been registered under its name, it must bear the adverse consequences of failing to meet its burden of proof.

Fourth, the Property Law establishes the principle of publicity of property rights, meaning that changes in property rights must be made known to the public through certain methods. The purpose is to enable third parties to be aware of changes in property rights, so as to prevent harm to third parties and ensure transaction safety. In this case, there is a cooperative development contract relationship between Chongli Company and Jiajia Company, and Chongli Company has the right to bring a separate action against Jiajia Company to assert rights arising from the cooperative development contract. However, where the evidence submitted by Chongli Company is insufficient to prove that it is the lawful construction party recorded in the relevant approval procedures, the facts of its investment, or its right of occupancy, merely relying on its cooperative development contract relationship with Jiajia Company does not qualify it as a lawful constructor under Article 30 of the Property Law. The original judgment, in finding that Chongli Company had obtained ownership of the houses involved based on lawful construction, applied the law incorrectly, and this court corrects that error.

In conclusion, the appeal grounds of Shaanxi Branch of Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd. are established and shall be upheld. In accordance with Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court rules as follows:

1. The civil judgment (No. [2015] Shaan-Min-Yi-Chu-Zi No. 00037) of the Shaanxi High People's Court is reversed;

2. All claims of Shaanxi Chongli Industrial Development Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

The case acceptance fees of the first and second instances are each RMB 42,800, totaling RMB 85,600, to be borne by Shaanxi Chongli Industrial Development Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Li Qi

Acting Judge: Xie Aimei
